person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: The racial in-group bias in empathic neural response to others' pain, and whether shifting a person's self-construal changes it.
span.quote: Recent neuroimaging findings indicate that people more strongly share racial in-group members’ painful feelings compared with those of out-group members

span.label: Cultures differ in how strongly people favour their own group's suffering - is the self-construal that distinguishes those cultures the thing actually doing the work?
span.quote: Although these findings uncovered cultural differences in parochial altruism and in-group bias in empathy, the underlying psychological and neural mechanisms remain unknown.

span.label: Shows the neural in-group bias is not fixed: priming an independent self-construal reduces it in insula, mid-cingulate and SMA, which makes self-construal a candidate cause rather than a correlate.
span.quote: Our findings suggest that shifting an individual’s self-construal leads to changes of his/her racial in-group bias in neural responses to others’ suffering.

span.label: mechanism
span.quote: Our findings suggest that shifting an individual’s self-construal leads to changes of his/her racial in-group bias in neural responses to others’ suffering.

span.label: racial in-group bias in empathy for pain
span.quote: This work tested the hypothesis that modifying self-construals, which differentiate between collectivistic and individualistic cultural orientations, affects in-group bias in empathy for perceived own-race vs other-race pain.

span.label: fmri
span.quote: By scanning adults using functional magnetic resonance imaging, we found stronger neural activities in the mid-cingulate, left insula and supplementary motor area (SMA) in response to racial in-group compared with out-group members’ pain after participants had been primed with interdependent self-construals.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: self-construal sets where the psychological boundary falls: interdependence draws the line between in-group and out-group, independence draws it between self and all others and so weakens the in-group/out-group split that produces biased empathy
span.quote: Our findings are consistent with a social-cognitive model of the link between self-construals and intergroup relationship ( Markus and Kitayama, 2010 ) that suggests that interdependent self-construals induce a strong boundary between in-group and out-group whereas independent self-construals define a strong boundary between the self and any others and lead to a weakened boundary between in-group and out-group.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: independent priming shifts cultural identity toward Western cultures, so Caucasian models are recategorised as in-group and their suffering draws a stronger neural response
span.quote: One possible account is that independent self-construal priming shifted our participants’ cultural identity toward Western cultures and Caucasian models were thus treated as in-group members, which in turn enhanced neural responses to their suffering.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: independent priming weakens race-based group affiliation between the Chinese participants and the Chinese models, dissolving the basis of the in-group advantage
span.quote: Alternatively, priming independent self-construals may weaken race-based group affiliation between Chinese participants and Chinese models shown in video clips.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: empathic concern generates altruistic motivation, so a bias in empathy toward in-group members produces parochial altruism in behaviour
span.quote: Because empathic concern produces altruistic motivation ( Batson, 2011 ), in-group bias in empathy may provide a mechanism of behavioral parochial altruism.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: an interdependent self organises behaviour by reference to others in one's relationships, which sharpens the in-group/out-group line
span.quote: In contrast, an interdependent schema of self organizes behavior immediately in reference to the thoughts and feelings of others with whom a person is in relationship and leads to significant ingroup–outgroup distinction.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: an independent self organises behaviour by reference to one's own thoughts, which weakens the group boundary and lets a person cross it easily
span.quote: According to Markus and Kitayama (2010) , an independent schema of self organizes behavior primarily in reference to an individual’s own thoughts and feelings and results in a weakened sense of in-group/out-group relationship so that people can move between in-group and out-group relatively easily.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: the route from bias to behaviour runs through empathy: empathic concern produces altruistic motivation, so a biased empathy yields a parochial altruism
span.quote: Because empathic concern produces altruistic motivation ( Batson, 2011 ), in-group bias in empathy may provide a mechanism of behavioral parochial altruism.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: self-construal is treated as temporarily shiftable, not as a fixed cultural trait - a 108-second reading task moves it
span.quote: Self-construal priming has been widely used in recent brain imaging studies that have shown that temporary shifts of self-construals influence multiple neurocognitive processes in the human brain

span.label: The two competing explanations offered for why independent priming shifted responses toward out-group faces are not yet tested
span.quote: Although these possible accounts should to be verified in future research, the findings of differential neural responses to racial in-group and out-group individuals raise an interesting issue, i.e. does priming independent compared with interdependent self-construals undermine behavioral parochial altruism?

span.label: The reduction of racial bias under independent priming does not license the conclusion that Westerners lack racial in-group bias
span.quote: Our finding that independent self-construal priming reduced the racial bias in neural responses to perceived pain in others in the MCC/SMA and insula does not necessarily indicate the absence of racial in-group bias in individuals from Western cultures.

span.label: The self-report measures showed no racial in-group bias at all, so the effect rests on the imaging measures
span.quote: The modulations of racial in-group bias in neural responses to perceived pain in others were confirmed in the ROI, whole-brain and ES analyses, though self-report did not show any racial in-group bias possibly due to the influences of social desirability.

span.label: One cultural sample: 30 Chinese university students, in a design whose logic is about differences between cultures.
span.quote: Thirty-two Chinese university students were recruited as paid volunteers.

span.label: The mechanism linking culture to bias was unknown going in, and the study offers a candidate rather than settling it.
span.quote: Although these findings uncovered cultural differences in parochial altruism and in-group bias in empathy, the underlying psychological and neural mechanisms remain unknown.

span.label: Race is operationalised as Asian versus Caucasian faces in short video clips, which is a narrow stand-in for a social category.
span.quote: consisting of 48 video clips showing faces of six Asian (three males) and six Caucasian models (three males) with neutral expressions who received painful (needle penetration) or non-painful (Q-tip touch) stimulation applied to the left or right cheeks

span.label: Markus and Kitayama's independent/interdependent self-construal distinction, imported as the cognitive variable that might explain a cultural difference in neural empathy
span.quote: According to Markus and Kitayama (2010) , an independent schema of self organizes behavior primarily in reference to an individual’s own thoughts and feelings and results in a weakened sense of in-group/out-group relationship so that people can move between in-group and out-group relatively easily.

span.label: confidence interval

span.label: After interdependent self-construal priming, watching a racial in-group member in pain produced stronger activity than an out-group member in the mid-cingulate cortex, left supplementary motor area and left insula.
span.quote: Specifically, we found that viewing racial in-group compared with out-group members in pain elicited stronger responses in the MCC, left SMA and insula when interdependent self-construals were primed.

span.label: Priming independent self-construals abolished that racial in-group bias in neural responses to others' pain.
span.quote: In contrast, the racial in-group bias in neural responses to perceived pain in others was eliminated when independent self-construals were primed.

span.label: Priming independent rather than interdependent self-construals both lowered the response to in-group members' pain and raised the response to out-group members' pain, although only the increased mid-cingulate response to out-group faces reached significance across priming conditions.
span.quote: The neural activity in all the ROIs showed a similar pattern that, relative to interdependent self-construal priming, independent self-construal priming tended to reduce the neural activity to racial in-group members’ pain but to increase the neural activity to racial out-group members’ pain, though the cross-priming comparison only confirmed a significant effect on the MCC activity to racial out-group members’ pain.

span.label: Subjective ratings of others' pain and of the observer's own unpleasantness showed no racial in-group bias, unlike the brain measures.
span.quote: Thus, self-report of one’s subjective feeling did not show racial in-group bias.

span.label: Participants' habitual (chronic) self-construal scores were unrelated to how much racial in-group bias their brain activity showed.
span.quote: Chronic self-construals measured from participants in this study did not correlate with patterns of their racial in-group bias in neural activity.

span.label: Across all conditions, seeing painful compared with non-painful stimulation applied to another person activated the mid-cingulate cortex, bilateral supplementary motor area, bilateral insula/inferior frontal gyrus, bilateral secondary somatosensory cortex, bilateral superior parietal and middle temporal gyri, and bilateral posterior cerebellum.
span.quote: The contrast of painful vs non-painful stimuli across all conditions revealed significant activations at a threshold of P < 0.05 (cluster-level corrected) in the MCC, bilateral SMA, bilateral insula/inferior frontal gyrus (IFG), bilateral second somatosensory cortex (SII), bilateral superior parietal gyrus (SPG), bilateral middle temporal gyrus (MTG) and bilateral posterior cerebellum ( Figure 1 and Table 2 ).

span.label: A whole-brain priming-by-race interaction, at a relaxed voxel threshold, located the same modulation in the left supplementary motor area, left inferior frontal gyrus and right temporo-parietal junction.
span.quote: However, using a voxel-level threshold of P < 0.001 and an extent threshold k > 20 voxels ( Lieberman and Cunningham, 2009 ), this analysis revealed significant activations in the left SMA (−3/26/52, k = 21), left IFG (−50/17/31, k = 23) and right temporo-parietal junction (51/−52/31, k = 26).

span.label: After interdependent priming, in-group pain produced stronger activity than out-group pain in mid-cingulate, left insula and SMA - the bias is present.

span.quote: Thus, 30 participants (16 males, 14 females; 18–27 years, mean ± s.d. = 22.6 ± 2.4 years) were included in data analyses.
